title: Why You Can See Through A Microwave Door

scenes.narration: Why can you see through a microwave door if the microwaves are supposed to stay trapped inside?
scenes.note: Bill's face is already pressed to the microwave at frame 0. The question is the hook.

beats.action: Bill nose-to-glass watching a plate rotate; microwave glow on his face
Bill leans back slowly, suspicious of his own kitchen
the plate inside completes a slow rotation; Bill tracks it with his eyes
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

angry orange energy dots pile up against the inside of the door and bounce back

scenes.narration: Because that black metal mesh is doing something clever.
scenes.note: Mina arrives. Mechanism scene begins — the mesh gets named as the actor.

beats.action: hard cut to the mesh filling frame; each opening is a clean hexagon
the mesh flashes teal and a label snaps onto it

scenes.narration: Microwave energy has a wavelength much larger than those tiny openings, so the conductive screen strongly blocks it from escaping.
scenes.note: The size comparison IS the explanation. Draw the wave enormous next to the holes.

beats.action: a fat orange sine wave draws itself across frame, far wider than the mesh openings
the orange wave takes a second run at the mesh and bounces again, harder

beats.action: the wave's width is measured against one opening; it does not come close to fitting
the openings pulse; the wave bumps them and bounces back with impact marks
the wave rebounds into the oven cavity; a BLOCKED stamp lands on the mesh

scenes.narration: Visible light has a vastly shorter wavelength, so light can pass through the holes and reach your eyes,
scenes.note: Same diagram, opposite outcome. Reuse the exact framing so only the wave changes.

beats.action: the rebounding wave rattles around the cavity, losing energy

beats.action: a thin bright teal wave draws itself, tiny beside the orange one
the small wave slips straight through an opening without touching the sides
the light lands in Bill's eye; his pupil catches a highlight

scenes.narration: which means the same door can behave like a window for you while acting like a barrier for the energy cooking your leftovers.
scenes.note: The door is split down the middle: window on Bill's side, barrier on the energy's side.

beats.action: camera pulls back; the door splits into two labelled halves
the left half stamps WINDOW in teal; light streams through it
the right half stamps BARRIER in coral; orange dots slam into it
inside, a sad plate of leftovers rotates, being cooked by the trapped energy

scenes.narration: Your microwave is basically wearing extremely nerdy sunglasses.
